title: Cloudflare Launches Public Certificate Authority to Secure the Web Against Quantum Threats - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Cloudflare (NET) plans to become a public Certificate Authority issuing classical and post-quantum Merkle Tree Certificates, acquiring GlobalSign root key material for legacy reach and applying to Chrome, Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs, with MTC issuance slated for Q1 2027.

insights.claim: Cloudflare intends to become a public Certificate Authority offering open, automated, high-scale issuance of both classical TLS certificates and post-quantum Merkle Tree Certificates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Expands Cloudflare's addressable market into Web PKI, competing with incumbent CAs and further entrenching its edge platform.

insights.claim: Cloudflare signed a definitive agreement to acquire publicly trusted Root CA key material from GlobalSign, trusted across browsers since 2012, expected to close within two months, while applying to the Chrome, Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Buying legacy root trust shortcuts the years-long path to ubiquitous device reach.

insights.claim: Cloudflare will be its own 'Customer Zero', routing its edge network — terminating TLS for over 20% of global web traffic — through the new CA stack.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Instant scale makes Cloudflare a major CA from day one, threatening incumbent CA economics.
insights.quote: terminating TLS for over 20% of global web traffic

insights.claim: Standard post-quantum signatures such as ML-DSA or SLH-DSA are up to 40x larger than classical RSA or ECDSA, threatening TLS handshake speed and flooding Certificate Transparency logs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQ migration imposes real network costs, creating demand for optimization by CDN/edge providers.
insights.quote: produce signatures up to 40× larger than classical RSA or ECDSA keys

insights.claim: Merkle Tree Certificates shift PKI from 'log what you issue' to 'issue by logging': the CA batches requests into an append-only Merkle tree, signs only the tree head, and servers present compact (<1 kB) inclusion proofs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An architectural change to Web PKI that Cloudflare co-authored in the IETF PLANTS group, giving it standards leverage.
insights.quote: MTCs redesign the PKI paradigm from “log what you issue” to “issue by logging.”

insights.claim: In trials with Chrome Beta 146 across Cloudflare domains, landmark-relative MTCs showed a 9% median TLS handshake speedup over classical signature chains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Post-quantum security that is faster than today removes a key objection to migration.
insights.quote: landmark-relative MTCs demonstrated a 9% net performance speedup at the median over classical signature chains

insights.claim: The CA uses an ACME-first stack forked from Boulder with mandatory RFC 9773 ARI renewal signaling, enabling zero-downtime rotation and instant mass revocations without site outages.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Automation lowers operational risk of mass revocation events that have historically caused outages.

insights.claim: Classical issuance begins after browser root approvals, while production Merkle Tree Certificate issuance is scheduled for Q1 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A dated catalyst for Cloudflare's post-quantum product line.
insights.quote: production Merkle Tree Certificate issuance is scheduled for Q1 2027

insights.claim: The initiative is aimed at combating 'harvest now, decrypt later' campaigns and aligning with emerging browser policies such as Chrome's Quantum-Resistant Root Program.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Browser policy changes could force CA ecosystem consolidation around PQ-capable providers.
